reader.decision: Approve the allowlist (PATH, HOME, HTTPS_PROXY, TINKERBOX_*) in runner/spawn.py in place of the two-name denylist edit.
reader.decision_reason: The denylist fails open, and it is how STRIPE_API_KEY leaked. The message says the allowlist matches the plugin contract, and the plugins it found need only HOME and HTTPS_PROXY. A plugin that needs another variable fails visibly, where a leak is silent.

reconstruction.problem: plugin_env in runner/spawn.py copies the whole runner environment and removes only three names (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN). STRIPE_API_KEY was added to the runner on 2 October and was not on that list, so it reached the feed-fetch plugin. On 24 October a debug request made feed-fetch print its whole environment to stderr, and a customer pasted that into a public ticket. The ticket exposed STRIPE_API_KEY and SENTRY_DSN. Selin Aydin rotated the key the same day.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Every new runner secret leaks to plugins until someone remembers to add it to the denylist. Separately, feed-fetch's debug dump prints the environment, which is poor practice, but the message says it needs no change.
reconstruction.fix: In runner/spawn.py, delete DENYLIST and the pop loop. Add ALLOW_EXACT = {PATH, HOME, HTTPS_PROXY} and ALLOW_PREFIX = 'TINKERBOX_'. plugin_env copies only matching names, then sets TINKERBOX_PLUGIN_DIR as before. The alternative is to add STRIPE_API_KEY and SENTRY_DSN to DENYLIST.
reconstruction.cost: A plugin that needs another variable fails until the name is added to the allowlist, and the message says this failure is visible. The denylist alternative costs two names and breaks no plugin, but it leaves every future secret exposed.

follow_up_questions: Is there any plugin outside this repository, or any unaudited plugin, that needs the full runner environment and cannot be checked this week?
reader.closing_answer: I approve the allowlist with PATH, HOME, HTTPS_PROXY and TINKERBOX_*, not the two-name denylist edit. The message does not say that any external plugin needs the full environment. If one turns up, I add its variable to the allowlist.
